CHAMPIONS

HCC All Stars Crowned Champions with Commanding 92-Run Victory Over Burloak Strikers in HDCL T25 Premier Final

NIAGARA FALLS, ON — Halton Cricket Club’s HCC All Stars captured the 2026 Hamilton and District Cricket League (HDCL) T25 Premier Division title on September 13 with a clinical 92-run win over Burloak Strikers at the NCC Ground Stadium.

Leading from the front, captain Gursewak guided his team with both bat and ball, anchoring a hard-fought first innings before a disciplined bowling attack dismantled the Strikers for just 94 runs.

Gursewak, Rohit, and Abhilash Set Imposing Target
Winning the toss and choosing to bat, HCC All Stars faced early pressure when opener Shubham was caught off Burloak skipper Nikhil in the opening over for 8.

Rohit and captain Gursewak steadied the innings with an aggressive 73-run stand. Rohit anchored the top order with 32 off 39 deliveries (3 fours), while Gursewak went on the attack, striking a 29-ball 42 laced with 3 fours and 3 sixes. Abhilash sustained the scoring rate with a blistering 24 off just 13 balls (2 fours, 2 sixes).

Burloak bowler Nammo sparked a middle-order fightback, finishing with figures of 4 for 24 across his five overs to remove Gursewak, Rohit, Abhilash, and Jaspreet. Despite late strikes from Retesh (3/41), lower-order contributions from Neel (16) and Ankur (12 off 7) carried HCC All Stars to a competitive 186 all out in 24.2 overs.

Relentless Bowling Attack Dismantles Strikers Chase
Defending 186, HCC All Stars seized control immediately with the ball and in the field. Rami bowled Nirav (5) in the third over, followed quickly by a run out of Vivek (6) executed by Shubham and wicketkeeper Neel to leave the Strikers at 24/2.

Gursewak introduced himself into the attack and struck in his first over, trapping opener Vijiram lbw for 10. Burloak captain Nikhil offered the lone resistance with a battling 26 off 24 deliveries, but his dismissal in the 11th over—caught by Gursewak off Gurbhej—triggered a fatal collapse. Burloak plummeted from 59/3 to 59/6 in the span of four deliveries: Nikhil caught by Gursewak off Gurbhej in the 10.4 over, Sourabh caught behind by Neel off Gurbhej for a duck in the 10.5 over, and Prasad bowled by Hardeep for 6 in the 11.1 over.

Hardeep soon removed Sumant (0) to finish with 2 for 19, while Gursewak maintained total control at the other end, taking 2 for 9 in 4 overs. Gurbhej polished off the tail to claim match-best bowling figures for HCC of 3 for 15 in 3.1 overs, trapping Vagish lbw in the 19th over to seal the championship.

Match Summary
HCC All Stars: 186 all out in 24.2 overs — Gursewak 42 (29), Rohit 32 (39), Abhilash 24 (13); Nammo 4/24 (5.0 ov), Retesh 3/41 (4.2 ov).
Burloak Strikers: 94 all out in 18.1 overs — Nikhil 26 (24), Vagish 11 (8), Vijiram 10 (17); Gurbhej 3/15 (3.1 ov), Gursewak 2/9 (4.0 ov), Hardeep 2/19 (4.0 ov).
Result: HCC All Stars won by 92 runs to win the 2026 HDCL T25 Premier Division Championship.

FINAL RESULT

HCC Northern Falcons Fall Short in Hard-Fought HDCL Premier 40 Overs Final After Sensational Campaign

OAKVILLE, ON — Halton Cricket Club’s HCC Northern Falcons concluded an extraordinary 2026 campaign as runners-up in the Hamilton and District Cricket League (HDCL) Premier 40 Overs Division on September 6, falling 51 runs short against Imperial Premier at the Sixteen Mile Sports Complex. Despite the heartbreak in the decider, our squad showed immense resilience, character, and skill to reach the pinnacle match of the competition.

Spirited Bowling Display Restricts Imperial to 186
After Imperial Premier won the toss and opted to bat, our bowling unit applied constant pressure against a deep batting lineup. Jay delivered an early breakthrough by trapping opposing captain Manpreet lbw for 28. Luv soon followed up by removing Shiven (6), caught neatly by Nakul.

Our captain Sameer led from the front with the ball, breaking through the middle order to claim 3 for 48 in his eight-over spell. His victims included Ninder (10), top-scorer Roshan (45), and Sukh (3). At the other end, Jay bowled with tremendous bite to finish with 3 for 35 in seven overs, including the crucial wicket of Pavneet (33).

Ishumanbir delivered a masterful spell of control in the later stages, taking 3 for 28 in seven overs to rip through the lower order—dismissing Surinder (13), Moneypal (8), and Divyanshu (7). Backed by sharp fielding—including three catches behind the stumps by Harpreet—our disciplined attack bowled Imperial Premier out for 186 in 38 overs, setting up a manageable target of 187.

Nakul Sparks Explosive Chase Before Middle-Order Collapse
Our chase began in breathtaking fashion thanks to an explosive assault from opener Nakul. Taking on the Imperial bowling attack from ball one, Nakul raced to a blistering half-century, smashing 50 runs off just 30 deliveries featuring 5 boundaries and 3 massive sixes at a strike rate of 166.67.

Nakul’s fireworks propelled us to a commanding 63 without loss inside the first seven overs. However, the momentum flipped dramatically when Nakul was caught off Divyanshu on the final delivery of the seventh over. Harpreet fell on the very next ball for 6, leaving us 63/2.

Ishumanbir provided steady resistance from number three, compiling a composed 22 off 24 deliveries (2 fours). Masroor fought hard with 15 off 24 balls in the middle order, but Imperial’s bowling tandem of Divyanshu (3/14), Manpreet (3/22), and Surinder (2/25) dried up the scoring opportunities and triggered regular wickets.

From 91/3, our lineup faced mounting pressure as the required run rate crept up. Despite late fight from captain Sameer, Shubham, Nitin, and Harsh, our innings was brought to a close at 135 all out in 32.3 overs.

Pride in a Memorable Season
While the final result was not the outcome we battled so hard for, reaching the HDCL Premier 40 Overs Final stands as a landmark achievement for Halton Cricket Club. Overcoming tough league stages, high-pressure playoff fixtures, and delivering strong performances against top-tier competition demonstrated the immense depth and talent within the Northern Falcons.

Our players, coaching staff, and supporters can look back on this season with immense pride as we build toward going one step further next summer.

Match Summary
Imperial Premier: 186/10 in 38.0 overs — Roshan 45 (81), Pavneet 33 (34), Manpreet 28 (28); Ishumanbir 3/28 (7.0 ov), Jay 3/35 (7.0 ov), Sameer 3/48 (8.0 ov), Luv 1/7 (2.0 ov).
HCC Northern Falcons: 135/10 in 32.3 overs — Nakul 50 (30), Ishumanbir 22 (24), Masroor 15 (24); Divyanshu 3/14 (6.3 ov), Manpreet 3/22 (8.0 ov), Surinder 2/25 (8.0 ov), Shiven 2/44 (7.0 ov).
Result: Imperial Premier won by 51 runs.

SEMI-FINAL THRILLER

David Slays Goliath: Underdog Falcons Stun Undefeated Raptors in HDCL Semi-Final

In an all-Halton Cricket Club clash that will be remembered for the ages, fourth-seeded HCC Northern Falcons pulled off a monumental upset, toppling the previously unbeaten league leaders, HCC Northern Raptors, by one wicket in the HDCL 40-Over Premier Division semi-final.

Entering the knockout clash, the Raptors appeared invincible after sweeping every match in the group stage to finish atop the table. The Falcons, sneaking into the playoffs in the fourth spot, were widely written off. What played out, however, was a classic David-versus-Goliath duel decided on the penultimate ball of the match.

The Falcons set the tone early with the ball, tearing through the Raptors’ formidable top order. Jay Shah (4/32) and skipper Sameer Verma (4/32) unleashed a devastating assault, reducing the Raptors to a staggering 7/4 inside six overs. Raptors captain Gurbhej Singh mounted a defiant counter-attack, smashing 39 off 35 deliveries alongside a patient 30 from Nirav Laheri. Yet, the Falcons never let off the pressure, bowling the tournament favorites out for just 130 in 31 overs.

Chasing a modest 131, the Falcons found the path to the final anything but smooth. The Raptors' bowling attack fought ferociously for every inch, sharing wickets across the board to trigger a tense collapse. Opener Shikhar Batta anchored the innings with grit, crafting a crucial 32 off 91 balls, supported by Masroor T’s brisk 24.

When captain Sameer Verma fell for a duck to leave the Falcons teetering at nine wickets down, the Raptors smelled an improbable escape. Enter Jay Shah. Capping off an extraordinary all-round performance, Shah kept his nerve under intense pressure, hitting an unbeaten 16 off 19 deliveries. Alongside a rock-solid Shubham Sharma (6*), Shah steered the Falcons across the finish line with just one ball to spare in the 40th over, sealing an unforgettable one-wicket victory.

With giant-killing bravado, the Falcons now advance to the HDCL Premier Division Final, having proved that regular-season records count for nothing once playoff cricket begins.

SEASON RECAP

Halton Cricket Club Scripts History: Record Four Teams Power Into 2026 HDCL Playoffs

Halton Cricket Club (HCC) has achieved a historic milestone in the 2026 Hamilton District Cricket League (HDCL) season, qualifying an unprecedented four squads for the postseason across the 40-Over and T25 Premier Divisions.

40-Over Premier Division: Raptors Dominate, Falcons Clinch Semis
The club’s 40-over campaign was highlighted by an unbeaten run from HCC Northern Raptors, captained by Gurbhej Singh. The Raptors finished atop the table with 105 points, posting a dominant 9–0 record (3 no-results) and an impressive net run rate (NRR) of +2.439.

Joining them in the semi-finals are Sameer Verma’s HCC Northern Falcons. In a fiercely contested battle for the top four, the Falcons secured 4th position with 55 points (5 wins, 4 losses, 3 no-results). Their +0.597 NRR proved decisive, edging out Oakville Eagles and MASS Niagara Premier on tiebreakers to lock in their playoff berth.

T25 Premier Division: All Stars and Icefield Jets Secure Quarter-Final Spots
HCC’s depth was equally evident in the T25 tournament, where two sides advanced to the quarter-finals:

HCC All Stars (Central Conference): Led by Gursewak Pandher, the All Stars sealed 2nd place with 80 points (7 wins, 3 losses, 2 no-results), powered by a massive +3.397 NRR.

HCC Icefield Jets (East Conference): Commanded by Gaurav Thakur, the Icefield Jets took 2nd place in the East with 85 points (6 wins, 3 losses, 3 no-results) and an NRR of +0.732, edging CSK Cholas on net run rate.

HCC Northern Strikers (West Conference): Captained by Rahul Chug, the Strikers fought through a challenging campaign in a stacked group, picking up 3 victories (30 points) and delivering strong competitive moments despite falling short of qualification.

With two squads contending for the 40-over championship and two advancing into knockout cricket in the T25s, Halton Cricket Club enters the postseason in pursuit of dual league titles.

COMMUNITY ADVOCACY

Club President Urges Burlington City Council to Expand Cricket Grounds as Demand Surges

BURLINGTON, ON — Local cricket advocates are calling on Burlington City Council to urgently prioritize and expand dedicated cricket facilities across the city, warning that current infrastructure falls drastically short of serving the region's rapidly growing cricket community.

Addressing council members during delegations on municipal recreation planning and facility usage, Harsh Singh, President of the Halton Cricket Club, delivered a passionate plea detailing the critical shortages facing the sport in Burlington.

A Sport in Need of Room to Grow
Burlington and the greater Halton region have experienced significant demographic shifts over the past decade, sparking unprecedented interest in cricket. Despite representing hundreds of active adult competitors and dozens of youth academy players, teams are left competing for scarce, multi-use green spaces.

“Cricket has been treated as an immigrant sport just because of the demographics that are involved in it, but that is not true. Cricket has a deep and rich history in Canada,” Singh noted to council, stressing that the sport deserves the same institutional respect and dedicated municipal infrastructure as traditional Canadian staples like baseball and hockey.

Singh highlighted that existing amenities—such as the pitch at Central Park, which overlaps with baseball outfield diamonds—create scheduling friction, maintenance conflicts, and severe seasonal constraints for both organized clubs and neighbourhood residents.

Key Advocacy Points Presented to Council
During his address, Singh underscored several key priorities necessary to support Burlington's cricket community:

Developing Dedicated, Standalone Grounds: Sharing outfields with existing baseball diamonds forces clubs into restrictive permit windows and exposes grounds to damage, necessitating fully dedicated pitches designed specifically for cricket dimensions.

Protecting Youth and Grassroots Programs: Local academies and junior programs are currently constrained by space, forcing Burlington youth to travel outside city lines to Oakville, Mississauga, or Milton just to practice and compete.

Minimizing In-Season Disruption: Singh urged the city to align future renovations and park maintenance schedules outside active league months (May through September) so players are not displaced mid-season.

Proactive Safety & Community Mitigation: While addressing neighbourhood concerns regarding stray balls and noise, Singh emphasized that organized leagues utilize controlled equipment, maintain later start times on weekends to respect quiet hours, and actively seek city partnership to implement proper safety netting and buffers.

Looking Ahead
With the city updating its parks and recreation master plans, Singh and fellow sporting delegates reiterated that expanding cricket facilities is not merely an athletic request, but an essential step toward inclusive municipal investment.

“The demand is already here, and it’s continuing to grow,” said Singh. “Our community isn't just looking for temporary fixes—we need sustainable grounds where future generations of Burlington cricketers can thrive.”
